subsystems.name: Post-quantum cryptographic primitives
subsystems.role: mathematical functions that resist attacks by both classical and quantum computers, used for key exchange and digital signatures.
parts: hash-based signatures for firmware or long-lived roots

subsystems.name: Key generation and storage
subsystems.role: creates and protects the long-term private keys that define an identity.
parts: hardware security module (HSM) with PQC support
secure element or trusted execution environment in devices

subsystems.name: Identity provisioning
subsystems.role: enrols users and issues quantum-safe credentials.
parts: certificate authority issuing PQC or hybrid certificates

subsystems.name: Authentication protocol
subsystems.role: proves identity using PQC signatures or key exchange without revealing the private key.
parts: session key establishment via PQC key encapsulation

subsystems.name: Client authenticator
subsystems.role: the user side that holds the private key and signs challenges.
parts: hardware security key (e.g., FIDO2 with PQC extensions)

subsystems.name: Verification infrastructure
subsystems.role: validates signatures and checks whether credentials are still trusted.
parts: certificate revocation lists or OCSP responders

buildSteps.title: Standardise the algorithms
buildSteps.detail: NIST selects and publishes standards for lattice-based key encapsulation and digital signatures, fixing parameter sizes and security levels.

buildSteps.title: Implement in cryptographic libraries
buildSteps.detail: Open-source and commercial libraries add the new primitives, with constant-time code to resist side-channel attacks.

buildSteps.title: Extend identity protocols
buildSteps.detail: TLS, FIDO2, X.509 and similar standards are updated to carry larger PQC keys and hybrid certificates.

buildSteps.title: Build hardware support
buildSteps.detail: HSMs, secure elements and TPMs gain PQC acceleration and enough secure storage for keys many kilobytes long.

buildSteps.title: Deploy certificate authorities
buildSteps.detail: CAs begin issuing PQC and hybrid certificates, so new credentials can coexist with legacy ones.

buildSteps.title: Roll out to clients
buildSteps.detail: Browsers, operating systems and authenticator apps add PQC support, often defaulting to hybrid modes.

buildSteps.title: Migrate servers and services
buildSteps.detail: Authentication servers accept PQC and hybrid logins, while gradually phasing out classical-only cryptography.

buildSteps.title: Audit and certify
buildSteps.detail: Independent testing checks correctness, side-channel resistance and interoperability before high-value systems switch over.

prerequisites.why: NIST has selected algorithms, but final standards and parameter sets are still being completed.
Not yet built, but encrypted data can be harvested today and decrypted later, making early migration urgent.
Lattice operations are heavier than RSA, so acceleration in HSMs and secure elements is needed for acceptable speed.
Protocols like FIDO2 and X.509 need extensions for PQC, which are still under development.
Hardware security modules and secure enclaves exist, but must be upgraded to hold larger PQC keys.

pathway.milestone: NIST PQC standardisation and early library implementations
pathway.unlocks: developers can experiment and build prototypes of quantum-safe identity.

pathway.milestone: Hybrid deployments in browsers and TLS (classical plus PQC)
pathway.unlocks: protection against harvest-now-decrypt-later without breaking compatibility.

pathway.milestone: PQC identity systems in enterprise and government pilots
pathway.unlocks: quantum-safe authentication for high-value systems and long-lived credentials.

pathway.milestone: Global migration to PQC-only identity infrastructure
pathway.unlocks: full resistance to quantum attacks across the internet.
